title: Force-field shield with impact ripples
purpose: Give three.js meshes an energy-shield look: a faint additive shell with a Fresnel edge, plus up to eight impact rings that spread from hit points across the surface and fade, fed through a ring buffer of uniform arrays with addHit. Use it for shields, barriers, bubbles and hit feedback.

engine.name: webgl2_browser
engine.notes: three.js r155 or later passed in as THREE (the fragment stage includes the tonemapping_fragment and colorspace_fragment chunks); only 0.186.1 was run.

contract.language: ECMAScript 2020 module; GLSL ES 3.00 through three.js ShaderMaterial

exports.name: createForceFieldMaterial
exports.summary: The transparent additive shield material; set uniforms.uTime.value every frame.

exports.name: addHit
exports.summary: Record a hit at a point in the mesh's own space at a time on the uTime clock; the oldest of eight slots is reused.

exports.name: rippleIntensity
exports.summary: CPU mirror of the ring: exp(-((d - speed * age) / width)^2) * (1 - age / lifetime)^2 * strength.

exports.name: FORCE_FIELD_MAX_HITS
exports.summary: 8, the number of hits the shader keeps.

exports.name: FORCE_FIELD_GLSL
exports.summary: GLSL function float rippleIntensity(float distanceFromHit, float age, float speed, float width, float lifetime, float strength).

exports.name: FORCE_FIELD_VERTEX
exports.summary: Object-space position for ripples, world position and normal for the edge.

exports.name: FORCE_FIELD_FRAGMENT
exports.summary: Base glow, Fresnel edge and the ripple sum.

options.name: fresnelPower
options.meaning: Exponent of the edge term; higher keeps the edge thinner.

options.name: doubleSided
options.meaning: Also draw the far side of the shell.

limits: Stylized, not a physical simulation. Ripple distance is the straight-line distance in the mesh's own space between the shaded point and the hit, which follows the surface only approximately (on a sphere of radius r the chord is shorter than the arc by about d^3 / 24r^2); rings jump across thin parts of concave meshes. Eight hits at most; a ninth replaces the oldest. Hits are stored in mesh space, so a scaled mesh scales its rings. Additive blending brightens whatever is behind; on a bright background the shield washes out. Only three.js 0.186.1 was run, in headless Chrome on SwiftShader WebGL 2.
technique_references: Gaussian ring travelling at constant speed with a quadratic fade
Ring buffer of uniform arrays for recent events
